F299 (spec loop, change an-absent-approver-is-not-named): the research's challenge holds in outcome, and R2 corrected R1's account of it. On claude 2.1.269, through the Hub's own argv and PTY spawn, in both spawn environments, F299's configuration still starts a turn and works until its first approval-needing call; there the harness process dies (exit 1, no result line, usage recorded as 'unavailable' although a model call was paid), showing the harness's own lines ('MCP server blocked by enterprise policy: agentweave' and 'approve_tool_call ... not found'). R1 had written 'exits 1 before any model call, spending nothing'; R2 found a model call and a Write attempt in every one of R1's own transcripts. 1b as written turns that into a turn that survives the refusal (from the second run): recorded, its refusals recorded, its model asking you to 'approve' a prompt that cannot appear. Answer the OPERATOR QUESTION at the top of proposal.md in one line: (a) 1b + --permission-prompts none on the approver-less spawn, gated on a known harness build (the refuting run's init line carries claude_code_version, so no separate probe, R3; 'no approval surface' 4/4, one of 4 still retried); (b) hand 1b back - what's missing is a Hub-authored sentence (research candidate 3, a new decision); or 1b as written. Also in the proposal, from the rounds: a per-run record of the server being injected AND of the harness reporting its start (else every new agent's first turn, or one typo in a runner's flags, loses a working approver); harness-decided refusals recorded for every Claude run, once per tool call via tool_use_id; and the shipped default-posture requirement gains the exception 1b decided (D11), so the spec stops contradicting itself. R3 (d4-r3) changed the mechanism, not the question: what counts as evidence against a harness is now what its init line said of the Hub's server (anything but 'connected'), because a server the harness gave up on or that crashed also completes a turn without reporting in; and the default-posture exception now promises only what the change delivers.

F336 (C, d1-drive): the app has no control that dispatches a review. A turn is a review only with review_task_id, and no UI code sends it. The card's 'Start <agent> on this' starts a WORK turn on a completed task, with no commit check and no 409. So the archived a-refused-review-leaves-nothing-behind human-only 6.1 and test-guide check 1 ('dispatch a review from the UI') can only be done through the API. Decide whether operators should hand-dispatch reviews in the app, which means a review item on the card that renders the refusal, or whether reviews stay flow-staffed and the guide is reworded to name the API.
